provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Art: portrait
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw a friend's portrait.
The pupils should be able to explain the proportions of the face.
Introduction:
We have learned about drawing shapes and lines. Today we will learn how to draw a proper portrait of our friend.
Content:
A portrait is a drawing of a person's face. To draw a good portrait, we must know the face proportions. The eyes are in the middle of the head. The nose is halfway between the eyes and chin. The mouth is halfway between the nose and chin. The head is oval-shaped. Use a pencil to lightly draw these lines before adding details.
Class activity:
Each pupil will choose a friend as a model. They will draw the friend's face following the correct proportions.
Evaluation questions:
What is a portrait?
Where should the eyes be on a face?
Why is it important to know face proportions?
Summary:
Today we learned how to draw a portrait with correct face proportions.

topics.title: Art: weaving
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to weave a simple mat.
The pupils should be able to create a two-colour pattern.
Introduction:
We have practiced making patterns with paper and colours. Today we will learn how to weave using threads to make a mat.
Content:
Weaving is making cloth or mats by crossing threads. We will use coloured threads to weave a small mat. First, we set up warp threads (vertical threads). Then we weave the weft threads (horizontal threads) over and under the warp threads. We can use two colours to make patterns like red and green.
Class activity:
The pupils will weave a small mat using two different coloured threads to create patterns.
Evaluation questions:
What is weaving?
What are warp threads?
How can you make a pattern with two colours?
Summary:
We learned how to weave a mat using two colours to make patterns.

topics.title: Music: solfa basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the solfa notes d r m f s.
The pupils should be able to identify the notes by their names.
Introduction:
We have been singing different songs in class. Today we will learn the basic musical notes that help us sing properly.
Content:
The solfa notes are do re mi fa sol. We write them as d r m f s. Do is the first note. Re is the second note. Mi is the third note. Fa is the fourth note. Sol is the fifth note. We can sing these notes in order to make the musical scale. Practice saying and singing each note clearly.
Class activity:
The class will practice singing the solfa scale together. The teacher will point to notes on the board and pupils will sing them.
Evaluation questions:
What is the first solfa note?
How many notes are in the basic scale?
Sing the solfa notes in order.
Summary:
We learned the basic solfa notes and how to sing the musical scale.

topics.title: Art: print making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a stamp printing.
The pupils should be able to make a repeat pattern.
Introduction:
We have made different patterns by drawing. Today we will learn how to make prints using stamps.
Content:
Print making is making prints from a stamp. We can cut a design from a potato or rubber to make a stamp. We dip the stamp in paint and press it on paper. To make a repeat pattern, we make the same stamp print again and again in rows. We can make patterns like circles or squares that repeat across the paper.
Class activity:
Each pupil will create a simple stamp from a potato and use it to make a repeat pattern on paper.
Evaluation questions:
What is print making?
How do you make a stamp print?
What makes a good repeat pattern?
Summary:
We learned how to make prints using stamps and create repeat patterns.

topics.title: Music: choir practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing in two groups.
The pupils should be able to try harmony singing.
Introduction:
We have practiced singing songs together. Today we will learn how to sing in groups and try harmony.
Content:
Harmony is when different groups sing different notes at the same time. We will divide the class into two groups. Group one will sing the main melody. Group two will sing a different note that fits with the melody. This makes the song sound richer. We start by singing simple songs like 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star' in two parts.
Class activity:
The class will be divided into two groups. Each group will practice their part separately, then try singing together.
Evaluation questions:
What is harmony?
What is the difference between melody and harmony?
How does singing in groups help?
Summary:
We learned how to sing in groups and try harmony singing.

topics.title: Art: sculpture
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a clay animal sculpture.
The pupils should be able to display their sculpture on a stand.
Introduction:
We have made different drawings and crafts. Today we will learn how to make sculptures using clay.
Content:
A sculpture is a three-dimensional art piece. We can make animal sculptures using clay. First, we roll the clay into a ball for the body. Then we add shapes for the head, legs, and tail. We use our fingers to smooth the clay and make it look like an animal. We let it dry and then we can paint it. We display sculptures on stands so everyone can see them well.
Class activity:
Each pupil will make a simple animal sculpture using clay and display it on a small stand.
Evaluation questions:
What is a sculpture?
What material do we use for making sculptures?
How do you make a clay animal?
Summary:
We learned how to make clay animal sculptures and display them.

topics.title: Drama: short play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plan and act in a short play.
The pupils should be able to create simple costumes.
Introduction:
We have read stories in class. Today we will learn how to turn a story into a play and act it out.
Content:
A play is a story acted out by people. We will plan a short play together. First, we choose a simple story. Then we assign roles to pupils. We practice saying our lines clearly. For costumes, we can use simple materials like cloth to show who is who. We practice moving on stage and speaking loudly so everyone can hear.
Class activity:
The class will plan and practice a short play about market day, with pupils making simple costumes from available materials.
Evaluation questions:
What is a play?
Why do we use costumes in plays?
How do you practice for a play?
Summary:
We learned how to plan and act in a short play with costumes.

topics.title: Art: cultural designs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify uli and adire patterns.
The pupils should be able to design their own cultural cloth.
Introduction:
We have learned about different patterns from our culture. Today we will learn about special Nigerian patterns and design our own cloth.
Content:
Uli patterns are traditional Igbo designs with curved lines. Adire patterns are Yoruba tie-dye designs with dots and lines. These patterns tell stories about our culture. We can create our own patterns using lines, dots, and shapes. We draw these patterns on paper to design our own cultural cloth.
Class activity:
Each pupil will create their own cultural design inspired by uli and adire patterns on a paper template of cloth.
Evaluation questions:
What are uli patterns?
Where do adire patterns come from?
How can you create your own cultural pattern?
Summary:
We learned about uli and adire patterns and designed our own cultural cloth.

topics.title: Music: concert practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to choose songs for a concert.
The pupils should be able to rehearse for a performance.
Introduction:
We have practiced singing different songs. Today we will learn how to prepare for a concert performance.
Content:
A concert is a musical performance for an audience. We will choose songs that we can sing well. We practice standing in straight lines. We sing clearly and together. We practice clapping at the right time. We also think about how to enter and exit the stage nicely. Everyone must know when to sing and when to be quiet.
Class activity:
The class will choose two songs to perform and practice them as if for a real concert.
Evaluation questions:
What is a concert?
Why do we practice for concerts?
How should we stand during a performance?
Summary:
We learned how to choose songs and rehearse for a concert.

topics.title: Revision and exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to display their artwork.
The pupils should be able to explain what they made.
Introduction:
We have made many different art pieces this term. Today we will prepare to show them to others.
Content:
An exhibition is when we show our artwork to others. We will arrange all our art pieces nicely in the classroom. We can put drawings on the wall and sculptures on tables. We write our names on our work. We practice explaining what we made and how we made it. We walk around quietly to see everyone's work.
Class activity:
The pupils will arrange their artwork around the classroom to create an exhibition space and practice explaining their pieces.
Evaluation questions:
What is an exhibition?
How do you arrange artwork for display?
Why is it important to explain your art?
Summary:
We learned how to prepare an exhibition of our artwork and explain what we made.
